It is submitted that victim (PW-1) has admitted in her examination-in- chief that her age is 32 years, she has passed M.Sc. (Biology) and has also completed her B.Ed.

At the time of the incident,
she was working as a guest lecturer in a government school.
She has admitted that she developed acquaintance with the accused in November, 2014 while they were travelling in a bus.
During this acquaintance, they came close and appellant had offered help to prepare Mathematics subject for competitive examination so that she can secure a government job.
4. According to the victim on 17th December, 2014, she was celebrating her birthday when she had again met the accused.
There accused had taken her to the house of his friend where he had touched her inappropriately and then asked her for physical favours.
Thereafter, her privacy was violated.
5. It is an admitted fact that till 4th April, 2016, victim and the appellant were in physical relationship.

Thus, it is pointed out that when statements of the victim, as contained in Ex.P-4, as were recorded before the concerned Magistrate are taken into consideration, then it was first establishment of physical relationship and subsequently assurance was given for marriage.

Thus, it is pointed out that since relationship was with the mutual understanding and in any case victim has admitted that her date of birth is 17.10.1985 and not 17.12.2024.
The story of prosecution that on the date of her birthday, she was celebrating her birthday with the accused and where she was inappropriately handled is not made out.
6. Learned counsel also submits that, in para 13 of her cross- examination, victim has admitted that she wanted to marry with the accused.
She has also stated that accused later on denied from marriage.

She has also admitted in para 19 that she had established physical relationship with the accused for about 2 years and did not inform this fact to anybody because she had a belief that the accused will marry her.
7. PW-2, mother of the victim, admits that if accused would not have refused to marry her daughter she would not have reported the matter to the police.

8. Thus, it is submitted that a consensual relationship between two adults without there being any breach of trust or unnecessary promise of marriage will not fall within the definition of rape and,
therefore, this is a fit case to record acquittal in favour of the appellant.
9. Reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra [2019(3) SCC 608]; Mahesh Damu Khare Vs. The State of Maharashtra & Anr. [2024(11) SCC 398]; Prashant Vs. Thus, it is submitted that all these judgments support case of the appellant and, therefore, a finding of acquittal may be recorded.
11. Learned Deputy Advocate General, Ms. Shweta Yadav, opposes the prayer.
She submits that merely age of the victim is not a sufficient circumstance to deduce a conclusion that she was a consenting party.
It is pointed out that in the name of coaching if privacy of the victim was violated by the appellant, then that will be a case for conviction as has been recorded by learned trial Court.

12. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident from the evidence given by PW-1, victim, that she came to know of the appellant while travelling in a bus in November, 2014.
According to her this incident took place on 17.12.2014 when she was allegedly celebrating her birthday.
This incident took place in the house of friend of the appellant as she later came to discover.
13. She has not stated that she was lured to the place of the friend of the appellant in the name of marriage to establish any kind of relationship.
14. As pointed out by Shri Anil Khare, learned senior counsel, her accompanying the appellant to an unknown place amounts to a tacit consent for relationship.

15. Law laid down in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra (supra)
which has been followed in subsequent decisions of the Supreme Court in the case of Mahesh Damu Khare Vs. The State of Maharashtra & Anr. (supra) and Prashant Vs. State of NCT of Delhi (supra) .
16.

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Supreme Court has noted that Section 90 of IPC does not NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:8344 5 CRA-7487-2021 define term "consent".
"Consent" based on a "misconception of fact" is not consent in the eye of law.
Thus, in case of woman engaging in sexual relations on false promise to marriage, her "consent" is based on "misconception of fact", and such sexual act(s) will amount to rape.

17. Thus, what is to be seen is that there has to be a promise to marry, that promise to marry should be false and intention of maker at the time of making promise itself was not to abide by it but to deceive woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations.
18.
In the present case, this aspect of promise to marry and that being false and intention of maker at the time of making promise itself to not to abide by such promise is not made out.
Even aspect of deception is not made out.
In fact, victim has admitted that she had seen the appellant in the company of another woman.
When she had called the appellant then he had refused to surrender to her wishes when she had lodged complaint.

sentences.text: Thus, it is evident that, firstly, initiation of physical relationship was not on the promise of marriage.
Since initiation of relationship was not on the promise of marriage, question of it being false does not arise.

Secondly, if the victim had any infatuation towards the appellant and surrendered herself to the wishes of the appellant or otherwise, resulting in culmination of a physical relationship that will not amount to either deception or making a false promise of marriage.
20. When tested from these aspects, then it is evident that both the victim and her mother have admitted that there was a crush of the victim towards the appellant.
She wanted to marry the appellant.
She had not said and, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:8344 6 CRA-7487-2021 unequivocal, terms that appellant wanted to marry her.

Thus, in the light of the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar (supra), so also Mahesh Damu (supra) and Prashant (supra), we are of the opinion that since there was no deception, no false promise to marry, provisions of Section 375 of IPC will not be attracted so to uphold the conviction.
21. Accordingly, this criminal appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence is hereby set aside and the appellant is acquitted of all the charges.
Appellant is on bail, his bail bonds are hereby discharged.
Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.
